_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run (npm run check:golden where-did-the-time-go) with dev backend up. Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, the_day_you_described non-empty array, what_made_it_feel_different non-empty array (guard keys). GUARDS: (1) the_day_you_described capped at 12 entries (soft prompt cap, not a hard array-length guard — this schema is much smaller than v1's, so max_tokens 3500 has real headroom; watch for truncation on 'this week' timeframe inputs with very long accounts). (2) no-inner-double-quote rule (prose quotes the user's own words). (3) NOT format-strict — every field is prose/arrays of prose, no numeric badges. (4) guard keys top-level the_day_you_described (array+length) and what_made_it_feel_different (array+length); the_biggest_mismatch and try_this_next_time are deliberately NOT guard-required. try_this_next_time can be JSON `null` by design (case 2 below) — the frontend's truthy check already hides the section, so this is NOT a bug if you see it. DO NOT reverse: the no-inner-quote rule; the non-required guard on the_biggest_mismatch/try_this_next_time; the null-allowed contract on try_this_next_time.
_meta.known_issues: 2026-09-14 v2 owner rewrite removed The Visible Day's you-think/likely-actual time pairs, The Invisible Hours, and honest_capacity entirely (v1 invented unmeasured minutes with no basis in the account). v2.1 added PRESERVE NUMERICAL RELATIONSHIPS, DON'T INFER ATTENTION OR CONTROL, DON'T CLAIM COMPLETE ACCOUNTING, EXPLAIN ONLY WHAT THE ACCOUNT SUPPORTS, and the try_this_next_time null contract. v2.2 (this round) added NO UNSUPPORTED DURATIONS (never estimate a vague period like 'two afternoons' into hours), NO VALUE JUDGMENTS (don't equate activity with productivity, don't adopt the user's own word 'wasted' as fact), DON'T INVENT THE YARDSTICK (never infer what would have made the period worthwhile), ALLOW UNEXPLAINED GAPS (say plainly when the account doesn't explain where time went), and NEUTRAL OBSERVATION (try_this_next_time describes what to notice without priming speculative possibilities) — also made session_label/session_tags facts-only. Removed the sole remaining post-result cross-ref ('Check your burnout risk' → Before the Crash); the tool now carries zero manual cross-refs by design (added to audit_v2-3-2.py's NO_CROSSREF set, same pattern as WhatsMyVibe). Verified live on case 3 below (a 'wasted afternoon'/'week disappeared' account, the closest real-world trigger for value-judgment and yardstick-invention failures): no invented hour estimates for the vague 'two afternoons,' the word 'wasted' is attributed to the user rather than adopted as the tool's own conclusion, and try_this_next_time stays neutral ('not to judge it, just to see what those afternoons actually contained'). Two soft residuals disclosed, not chased further: session_label used the word 'disengaged' (echoes the DON'T INFER ATTENTION OR CONTROL banned-state list, even though the user didn't use that word), and the_biggest_mismatch's closing line introduced 'personal projects' as something the user 'normally measures against' — a yardstick the user never actually stated.

input.dayDescription: Um 8 mit Kaffee und E-Mails angefangen. Standup um 9. Wollte den Quartalsbericht schreiben, wurde aber in einen Slack-Thread über eine Kundeneskalation gezogen, das hat bestimmt eine Stunde gedauert. Mittagessen gegen 12:30. Nachmittags ein 1:1 mit meiner Chefin das überzogen hat, dann war ich glaube ich bis 4 in Calls. Habe eine Stunde an Folien für das morgige Review gearbeitet. Gegen 17:30 Schluss. Habe das Gefühl nichts Wichtiges geschafft zu haben.
input.perceivedBreakdown: Ich fühle mich als hätte ich nichts geschafft, aber ich war den ganzen Tag beschäftigt

the_day_you_described.note: Slack-Thread über Kundeneskalation – wollte am Quartalsbericht arbeiten, wurde aber hineingezogen
Calls (nach eigenem Eindruck durchgehend oder mit wenig Lücke nach dem 1:1)

what_made_it_feel_different: Der Quartalsbericht – die Aufgabe, die du dir vorgenommen hattest – wurde durch die Kundeneskalation komplett ersetzt, nicht unterbrochen. Das war eine große, geplante Arbeit, die nicht stattgefunden hat.
Der Nachmittag war vollständig durch Meetings geblockt: das 1:1 lief über, dann direkt Calls bis 16:00. Es gab keinen zusammenhängenden Block, um an etwas Größerem zu arbeiten.
Die Folien für das morgige Review sind echte Arbeit und erscheinen oft klein in der Rückschau, weil sie dokumentieren statt zu schaffen – aber sie nahmen trotzdem eine Stunde ein und waren notwendig.
Zwischen dem 1:1 und den Calls liegt ein verschwommener Übergang – unklar, wann das eine endete und die anderen begannen, was das Gefühl von Zersplitterung verstärkt.
output.the_biggest_mismatch: Du beschreibst einen Tag voller Aktivität von 8:00 bis 17:30, aber das einzige Großprojekt, das du dir vorgenommen hattest – der Quartalsbericht – fand nicht statt. Stattdessen waren es Meetings, Kundeneskalation und Folien. Der Tag war voll, aber nicht mit dem, das du zählen würdest.
output.try_this_next_time: Notiere morgen kurz, wenn ein geplanter Block (wie dein Quartalsbericht) durch etwas Dringendes ersetzt wird – schreib nur das Wort und die ungefähre Zeit auf. Nach einer Woche kannst du sehen, wie oft das passiert und zu welchen Tageszeiten. Das zeigt, ob es ein Muster gibt oder eher zufällig ist.

input.dayDescription: Slept in until 10. Made breakfast. Read a book for a couple hours. Went for a walk in the afternoon. Cooked dinner and watched a movie. Went to bed around 11.

the_day_you_described.note: Read a book for a couple hours

what_made_it_feel_different: No commitments or schedule — the day was shaped entirely by your own choices, each activity flowing into the next without external interruption.
A clear sequence of distinct activities with visible transitions: reading had a defined block; walking was clearly separate; dinner and a film occupied the evening together.
output.the_biggest_mismatch: None apparent. The account describes a coherent day with no stated feeling of fragmentation, lost time, or mismatch between what you intended and what happened.

input.dayDescription: Worked Monday through Friday, roughly 9-6 each day, but at least two of those days had a wasted afternoon where I was technically at my desk but not really working. Went to the gym twice instead of my usual four times. Had dinner with a friend Wednesday, cancelled plans Thursday because I was too tired. Weekend errands somehow ran over into Monday morning. Cant point to one big thing I accomplished outside of my actual job.
input.perceivedBreakdown: I feel like the whole week disappeared and I have nothing to show for the parts that werent work

the_day_you_described.time: At least two afternoons during the week (day unspecified)
the_day_you_described.note: Technically at desk but not working — user's own description
Twice during the week instead of usual four times
Planned evening cancelled — user reports being too tired
Weekend errands ran over into this time
User cannot point to one substantial accomplishment in this time

what_made_it_feel_different: Two full afternoons during work hours were spent at your desk without actual work — that's a visible gap between time and output within the structure you normally count as productive.
Gym dropped from four to two visits; Thursday plans cancelled due to fatigue — the week contained fewer of the things you usually do outside work than you expected.

The account describes what didn't happen (no substantial non-work accomplishment, cancelled plans, missed gym sessions) more clearly than what did — which may be why the week feels like it disappeared despite being full of scheduled time.
output.the_biggest_mismatch: You have 50+ work hours accounted for (9-6, five days), plus dinner Wednesday and two gym visits, plus weekend errands bleeding into Monday. The mismatch is not missing hours — it's that accomplishment outside of 'actual job' is invisible to you, while the work hours themselves are spent partly disengaged. The week didn't disappear because it was empty; it disappeared because the parts you'd normally measure yourself against (gym consistency, personal projects, evening plans that stick) contracted or stalled.
output.try_this_next_time: When you notice yourself at your desk in one of those disengaged stretches, write down what you were doing instead — not to judge it, just to see what those afternoons actually contained. This tests whether the pattern is truly 'nothing' or whether specific small things are happening but not registering as accomplishment.
output.session_label: Work week — two disengaged afternoons, fewer gym visits, plans cancelled
